rationale: The answer never mentions that PostgreSQL actually shipped this exemption in PG14 (commit d9d076222f) and reverted it in 2022 (commit e28bb88519) due to index corruption risk; instead it frames the current exclusion of CIC/REINDEX CONCURRENTLY from the vacuum horizon as 'already deliberately not done,' implying no such attempt was ever made — a direct contradiction of the record and a forbidden claim. The failure-mode mechanism (HOT pruning missing rows during CIC's snapshot-held scan) is correctly described, satisfying required fact 2, but required fact 1 (tried-and-reverted history) is absent and contradicted.
required_missing: That the ignore-CONCURRENTLY-in-horizon change was implemented and shipped in PG14 (commit d9d076222f) and then reverted (commit e28bb88519) in 2022
contradictions: "No. This is already deliberately not done..." implies the exemption was never attempted/shipped, when the record shows it was implemented in PG14 and later reverted
